entries.title: The Run
body: Explore rooms, survive fights, claim rewards, and push deeper toward the next boss.
Held embers travel with the run until banked, spent, recovered, or lost.

entries.title: Map and Rooms
body: Revealed exits show where you can travel next. Cleared rooms stay available as routes.
Combat, campfire, merchant, treasure, relic, and boss rooms each change the next choice.

entries.title: Character and Loadout
body: Equipment, attuned magic, item slots, relics, and progression stats shape your deck.
Most loadout changes happen outside combat, including pre-battle and campfire moments.

entries.title: Rewards
body: After combat, choose a card, take healing, or claim other room rewards when offered.
New magic cards enter reserve first; attune them from the character sheet to add them to the active deck.

entries.title: Relics
body: Relics are passive run modifiers. Some trigger in combat, some change card values, and some alter rewards.
Hover relic badges in the top HUD for their current text.

entries.title: Combat Board
body: Cards resolve on the tile board. Movement, range, line of sight, enemy positions, traps, and terrain all matter.
Select a card to preview legal targets and the projected result before committing.

entries.title: Turn Clock
body: Each card adds time. Lower total time means your next turn returns sooner.
The turn clock at the top previews who acts now and who is coming next.

entries.title: Card Plays
body: You normally get a limited number of card plays each player turn.
Some cards, kills, and relics can add extra plays before enemies act.

entries.title: Health and Defenses
body: Damage hits block first, then stoneskin, then health unless an effect says otherwise.
Block is temporary. Stoneskin is sturdier and persists until broken.

entries.title: Targeting
body: Melee targets nearby tiles. Ranged and area cards check range, sight, and pattern rules.
Forced movement needs a clear line and can slam targets through danger.

entries.title: Fatigue
body: When the draw pile empties, the discard pile reshuffles and fatigue can bite into health.
Thin decks cycle quickly. Watch the pile counters during long fights.

entries.title: Traps
body: Traps trigger when a unit enters their tile. Their element can add damage or control pressure.
Path previews mark danger before you move.

entries.title: Elemental Intensity
body: Elemental rooms build a shared intensity value. Some cards spend it, require it, or grow stronger from it.
Intensity belongs to the room, not to one card.

entries.title: Lightning Strikes
body: Lightning strikes choose several tiles and threaten repeated shock damage.
Watch the previewed danger pattern before ending your turn near a storm caller.

entries.title: Summons
body: Some enemies spend an action to call additional creatures into the fight.
Summoned enemies still take turns, block paths, and can add their own Grimoire entries.

entries.title: Melee
body: Melee attacks hit close targets. Position first, then strike.

entries.title: Ranged
body: Ranged attacks can hit distant targets if range and line rules allow it.

entries.title: Area Attack
body: Area attacks use a tile pattern. Some patterns rotate before you commit.

entries.title: Move
body: Move through reachable passable tiles. Enemies, illusions, terrain, and traps can shape the path.

entries.title: Blink
body: Blink relocates directly to a legal tile instead of walking a path.

entries.title: Block
body: Block absorbs damage before health. It is best used when enemies are about to act.

entries.title: Stoneskin
body: Stoneskin is persistent armor. It absorbs damage across turns until broken.

entries.title: Heal
body: Heal restores health up to maximum health. Some heals exhaust or burn the card after use.

entries.title: Draw
body: Draw adds cards to hand, limited by hand size.

entries.title: Card Play
body: Card play effects add temporary plays for the current player turn.

entries.title: Illusion
body: Illusions are decoys with health. Enemies can target and destroy them.

entries.title: Immobilize
body: Immobilize prevents movement for the rest of the affected turn.

entries.title: Exhaust
body: Exhausted cards leave the deck for the rest of combat.

entries.title: Health Cost
body: Health cost is paid when the card is played. It can be worth it, but it is real damage.

entries.title: Pierce
body: Pierce damage bypasses block and stoneskin without removing them.
It is strongest against armored enemies and dangerous when enemies use it on you.

entries.title: Bleed
body: Bleed opens before the affected unit moves or attacks, then clears after the next turn.
Plan around it when a card or enemy intent adds a wound.

entries.title: Burn
body: Burn deals fire damage over time, then decays.
Stacking burn pressures high-health targets and punishes long fights.

entries.title: Poison
body: Poison is delayed damage. It lands after its countdown instead of immediately.

entries.title: Freeze
body: Freeze prevents the affected unit from acting on its next turn.

entries.title: Shock
body: Shock disrupts the affected unit's next action.

entries.title: Expose
body: Expose makes the next hit against the target deal extra damage.

entries.title: Sunder
body: Sunder breaks block and stoneskin before damage lands.

entries.title: Chain
body: Chain jumps to additional nearby enemies after the first hit.

entries.title: Push
body: Push forces the target away. Forced movement can improve position or shove targets into danger.

entries.title: Pull
body: Pull forces the target closer. Use it to break lines, set up areas, or drag enemies through hazards.

entries.title: Consume
body: Consume removes an item card from the run after it is used.

entries.title: Tunnel Crawler
body: Fast close-range predator that closes distance and opens bleed wounds.
It has modest health, but its short clock can punish slow turns.

entries.title: Ash Acolyte
body: Ranged caster that mixes ash bolts, self-preservation, and draining pressure.
Keep cover, line of sight, and incoming intent timing in mind.

entries.title: Bone Harrier
body: Mobile ranged skirmisher with pierce and bleed pressure.
It often attacks while repositioning, so corners and approach paths matter.

entries.title: Ash Warden
body: Durable front-line guard with heavy melee, block, and close area pressure.
Pierce, sunder, forced movement, or focus fire help crack it cleanly.

entries.title: Cinder Ooze
body: Fire-locked ooze that can split into droplets when killed.
Clear space and plan the follow-up before finishing it.

entries.title: Cinder Droplet
body: Small ooze fragment spawned by larger cinder oozes.
Droplets are weaker, but several can steal board space at the wrong moment.

entries.title: Bile Bloomer
body: Earth-locked controller that spreads poison and expose pressure.
Its delayed damage rewards decisive positioning and quick target priority.

entries.title: Chainbound Gaoler
body: Air-locked jailer that pulls, pushes, and restricts movement.
Watch forced movement lines before committing fragile positions.

entries.title: Grave Surgeon
body: Support enemy that heals or guards injured allies.
Interrupt it early or expect wounded enemies to stay relevant.

entries.title: Frostglass Lancer
body: Ice-locked striker that threatens freeze and long reach.
Do not let it set up clean lines into your next turn.

entries.title: Zekarion, the Raging Tempest
body: Boss creature that commands storms, summons wisps, and pressures broad areas.
Track the clock, clear adds, and avoid giving the tempest a clustered board.

entries.title: Lightning Wisp
body: Summoned lightning minion with disruptive shock pressure.
Wisps are fragile, but leaving them alive can steal clean turns.
